info.description: CRUD API for records stored in PostgreSQL.
info.title: Records CRUD API

post.description: There is no password: knowing the email of a user created with POST /auth/users is enough (development only, no proof of ownership). On success, sets an HttpOnly "session" cookie (SameSite=Strict) that the browser sends on later requests, and returns the user. Accounts can only sign in with the method they were created with (403 for google/github accounts). An unknown email returns 401. After 5 failed attempts per email and IP, 429 for 15 minutes.
Ends the current session and clears the cookie. Requires a session.

Needs no session. Creates the organisation (name unique, ignoring case) with an "admin" and a "member" group, and its first admin user from admin_name and admin_email, in one step: the email must not be registered yet (409), and nothing is created if any part fails. Personal email providers (gmail, yahoo, ...) are rejected. The admin signs in with POST /auth/login.

Needs no session. organisation_id is required: the user gets the basic "member" role in that organisation (404 if it doesn't exist). Returns the created user. There is no password; the user signs in with POST /auth/login using the email. Personal email providers (gmail, yahoo, ...) are rejected.

get.description: Returns only the groups in the given organisation (an empty list if it has none).
get.summary: List the groups of an organisation

post.description: Returns the new group, including its ID. Names are lower-cased, must start with a letter, and are unique within the organisation.
post.summary: Create a group in an organisation

put.description: Sets the group's organisation and name (both required). The name must be unique within the organisation. A group that has users cannot be moved to another organisation (409).

delete.description: Fails with 409 while the group still has users; move them with the assign-group endpoint first.

get.description: Returns the name and email of every user in the group (an empty list if the group has no users).
get.summary: List the users in a group

get.description: The organisation of the signed-in user; no id is needed. 404 for a user without an organisation. Requires a session.

put.description: Admins only (403 for members). The new name must be unique, ignoring case. Requires a session.

delete.description: Admins only (403 for members). PERMANENTLY deletes the organisation, its groups, all its users (the caller included) and all their records, in one transaction. confirm_name must be the organisation's exact name (400 otherwise). The users' sessions stop working immediately. Requires a session.

get.description: Returns only the records that belong to the given user (an empty list if they have none).
get.summary: List the records of a user

post.description: The record belongs to the user given by user_id (404 if the user doesn't exist).
post.summary: Create a record for a user

put.description: Changes the name and email (work email only). The group is changed with the assign-group endpoint.

delete.description: Fails with 409 while the user still has records; delete those first.

put.description: The group must exist (404) and belong to the organisation stored on the user (400 otherwise).
put.summary: Assign a group to a user

group_id.description:
GroupID is the user's group, which always belongs to OrganisationID (the
database enforces it with a composite foreign key). A user without an
organisation has both as 0 (NULL in the database, omitted from JSON).

signup_method.description: SignupMethod is how the user was created (SignupMethod* constants).
